object.title: Coefficientwise minimality conjecture for standard orientations of bipartite graphs
object.statement: Let ${\mathcal{G}}$ be a bipartite graph, and consider its facet graphs and the two standard orientations of ${\mathcal{G}}$. For each facet graph, take its interior polynomial. **Standard-orientation minimality conjecture.** Among the facet graphs of ${\mathcal{G}}$, the two standard orientations of ${\mathcal{G}}$ have a coefficientwise minimal interior polynomial. This conjecture predicts a coefficientwise extremal property for the interior polynomials associated with facet graphs and remains open.
object.source_name: Tamás Kálmán and Lilla Tóthmérész, “Ehrhart theory of symmetric edge polytopes via ribbon structures”, arXiv:2201.10501 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.10501

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2022).

object.title: Harrington et al.'s divisibility conjecture for modulo-dependent chip-collecting games
object.statement:
Let $m$ and $n$ be positive integers with $m\mid n$, and let $a<b<\min\{m,n\}$. Consider the random walk on $\mathbb{Z}_m\times\mathbb{Z}_n$ whose moves are $(+a,+b)$ and $(+b,+a)$, with winning positions determined by the game. **Harrington et al.'s divisibility conjecture.** If all winning positions are of the form $(0,y)$, then

$$
m\mid(b^2-a^2).
$$

This conjecture concerns when the winning positions in the extended modulo-dependent game have a prescribed form. The supplied source does not state whether it has been resolved.
object.source_name: Joshua Harrington, Xuwen Hua, Xufei Liu, Alex Nash, Rodrigo Rios and Tony W. H. Wong, “Probabilistic chip-collecting games with modulo winning conditions”, arXiv:2201.10506 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.10506

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2022).

object.title: The chromatic quasisymmetric function conjecture for directed trees
object.statement:
Let $\overrightarrow{G}$ and $\overrightarrow{H}$ be directed trees, and let $X_{\overrightarrow{G}}(\mathbf{x},t)$ denote the chromatic quasisymmetric function of a directed graph. **The chromatic quasisymmetric function conjecture.** If $\overrightarrow{G}$ and $\overrightarrow{H}$ are not isomorphic, then

$$
X_{\overrightarrow{G}}(\mathbf{x},t)\neq X_{\overrightarrow{H}}(\mathbf{x},t).
$$

This is a natural quasisymmetric analogue of Stanley's conjecture that the chromatic symmetric function distinguishes trees; it was previously stated as a question by Alexandersson and Sulzgruber. The conjecture is open.
object.source_name: Jean-Christophe Aval, Karimatou Djenabou and Peter R. W. McNamara, “Quasisymmetric functions distinguishing trees”, arXiv:2201.11763 (2023).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.11763

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2022).

object.title: The principal specialization conjecture of Loehr and Warrington for trees
object.statement:
For a graph $G$, let $X_G(\mathbf{x})$ denote its chromatic symmetric function, and for a positive integer $n$ specialize the variables by $x_i=q^{i-1}$ for $1\leq i\leq n$ and $x_i=0$ thereafter. **Loehr–Warrington's principal specialization conjecture.** The polynomial

$$
X_G(1,q,q^2,\ldots,q^{n-1})
$$

distinguishes trees with at most $n$ vertices. This conjecture is stronger than Stanley's conjecture, since an affirmative answer would imply that the full chromatic symmetric function distinguishes trees. The source presents it as a recent conjecture of Loehr and Warrington; its general status is open.
object.source_name: Jean-Christophe Aval, Karimatou Djenabou and Peter R. W. McNamara, “Quasisymmetric functions distinguishing trees”, arXiv:2201.11763 (2023).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.11763

object.title: The Third Borwein conjecture at modulus five
object.statement:
For a positive integer $n$, define the finite $q$-Pochhammer symbol $(q;q)_r:=\prod_{j=1}^{r}(1-q^j)$ and

$$
S_n(q):=\frac{(q;q)_{5n}}{(q^5;q^5)_n}.
$$

**Third Borwein conjecture.** The sign pattern of the coefficients in the expansion of $S_n(q)$ is $+----+----+----\cdots$, with the convention that zero coefficients may be regarded as either sign. The source discusses an approach to this conjecture but does not establish the full assertion.
object.source_name: Chen Wang and Christian Krattenthaler, “An asymptotic approach to Borwein-type sign pattern theorems”, arXiv:2201.12415 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.12415

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2022).

object.title: Mészáros–Setiabrata–St. Dizier interval-support conjecture for Grothendieck polynomials
object.statement: Let $S_n$ be the symmetric group, let $\omega\in S_n$, and let $p_1(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ and $p_2(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ be monomials with nonzero coefficient in the Grothendieck polynomial $\mathfrak{G}_{\omega}$ such that $p_1$ divides $p_2$. **Mészáros–Setiabrata–St. Dizier's interval-support conjecture.** Every monomial $q(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ satisfying $p_1\mid q$ and $q\mid p_2$ also has nonzero coefficient in $\mathfrak{G}_{\omega}$. This predicts that the support of each Grothendieck polynomial is order-convex under divisibility; the source presents it as a conjecture about support, with no resolution supplied.
object.source_name: Elena S. Hafner, “Vexillary Grothendieck Polynomials via Bumpless Pipe Dreams”, arXiv:2201.12432 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.12432

object.title: Dijoin-clutter tau equals two conjecture
object.statement:
Let $(D=(V,A),w)$ be a weighted digraph, and let $\mathcal{C}(D,w)$ be its clutter of minimal dijoins. Suppose that $\mathcal{C}(D,w)$ is minimally non-packing.

**Dijoin-clutter $\tau=2$ conjecture.** The weighted digraph $(D,w)$ has a dicut of weight two.

This is presented as the weighted-dijoin specialisation of the $\tau=2$ conjecture for clutters. The supplied text does not state a resolution.
object.source_name: Ahmad Abdi, Gérard Cornuéjols and Michael Zlatin, “On packing dijoins in digraphs and weighted digraphs”, arXiv:2202.00392 (2023).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.00392

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of February 2022).

object.title: Linear-size total-variation approximation for the uniform infinite cubic planar graph
object.statement:
Let $(\mathsf{C}_n)_{n\in 2\mathbb{N}}$ be the random cubic planar graph with $V_n$ vertices, and let $\mathcal{D}_i(\mathsf{C}_n)$ and $\mathsf{D}(i)$ denote the associated degree quantities. For a given $\delta$ satisfying

$$
0<\delta<\frac{3\kappa}{2},
$$

**Linear-size approximation conjecture.** As $n\in 2\mathbb{N}$ tends to infinity,

$$
d_{\mathrm{TV}}\left(\left(\mathcal{D}_i(\mathsf{C}_n)\right)_{1\le i\le \min(\lfloor\delta n\rfloor,V_n)},\left(\mathsf{D}(i)\right)_{1\le i\le\lfloor\delta n\rfloor}\right)\to 0.
$$

This conjectures that the independent approximation established for sublinearly many indices remains valid for a positive linear proportion of the graph. The parser gives no resolution evidence, so the status of this approximation remains open.
object.source_name: Benedikt Stufler, “The Uniform Infinite Cubic Planar Graph”, arXiv:2202.00592 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.00592

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2022).

object.title: Non-periodicity conjecture for partitions into integers congruent to one modulo three
object.statement:
Let

$$
A=\{3n+1:n\in\mathbb{N}\}.
$$

For each $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $f_{A,n}(t)$ be the $n$-th $A$-partition polynomial, and let $\operatorname{sign}(f_{A,n}(-1))$ be its sign. **Non-periodicity conjecture.** The sequence

$$
\bigl(\operatorname{sign}(f_{A,n}(-1))\bigr)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}
$$

is not periodic.
This is posed as an example of sign behaviour that may fail to be periodic, contrasting with the eventually periodic cases established elsewhere in the paper.
object.source_name: Filip Gawron and Maciej Ulas, “Signs behaviour of sums of weighted numbers of partitions”, arXiv:2202.05221 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.05221

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2022).

object.title: The semigroup representation conjecture for generalized Petersen graphs
object.statement:
Let $G(n,k)$ be a generalized Petersen graph. A **semigroup graph** is a graph admitting a Cayley representation by a semigroup. **The semigroup representation conjecture.** Every generalized Petersen graph is a semigroup graph.

This asks whether the entire generalized Petersen family admits semigroup Cayley representations. The source states that the question remains open, while noting that the first cases $G(7,2)$ and $G(7,3)$ require a connection set of size $3$ in the monoid setting.
object.source_name: Ignacio García-Marco and Kolja Knauer, “Beyond symmetry in generalized Petersen graphs”, arXiv:2202.06785 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.06785

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2022).

object.title: Gedeon's equivariant Kazhdan–Lusztig coefficient bound for matroids
object.statement:
Let $M$ be a matroid of rank $k$ on the ground set $E$, and let $W$ be a finite group acting on $E$ and preserving $M$. Let $U_{k,E}$ denote the uniform matroid of rank $k$ on $E$, and let $P_M^W(t)$ be the equivariant Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial of $M$. Coefficients are compared as virtual representations of $W$.

**Gedeon's conjecture.** The coefficients of

$$
P_{U_{k,E}}^W(t)-P_M^W(t)
$$

are honest, rather than virtual, representations of $W$.

Equivalently, the equivariant Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial of any matroid should be coefficientwise bounded above by that of the uniform matroid of the same rank on the same ground set. The conjecture is unpublished, and the source gives no resolution status.
object.source_name: Trevor Karn, George Nasr, Nicholas Proudfoot and Lorenzo Vecchi, “Equivariant Kazhdan-Lusztig theory of paving matroids”, arXiv:2202.06938 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.06938

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2022). “In higher degrees, the conjecture remains open.”

object.title: The perimeter bound for triangular-grid billiards
object.statement:
Let $P$ be a grid polygon. Write $\operatorname{perim}(P)$ for the number of boundary panes of $P$ and $\operatorname{cyc}(P)$ for the number of cycles in its associated permutation, equivalently the number of light-beam trajectories in the associated billiards system.

**Perimeter conjecture.** If $P$ is a grid polygon, then

$$
\operatorname{perim}(P)\geq 4\operatorname{cyc}(P)-2.
$$

The conjecture proposes a sharper lower bound than the proven inequality $\operatorname{perim}(P)\geq \frac{7}{2}\operatorname{cyc}(P)-\frac{3}{2}$. The authors state that the existing bound is not tight based on examples, but no resolution of the conjectured bound is given here.
object.source_name: Colin Defant and Pakawut Jiradilok, “Triangular-Grid Billiards and Plabic Graphs”, arXiv:2202.06943 (2023).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.06943

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2022).

object.title: The globally rigid graph bridge conjecture
object.statement: Let $G$ be a globally rigid graph in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and let $e$ be an edge such that $G-e$ is not globally rigid. An edge is an **$\mathcal{R}_{d+1}$-bridge** when its deletion lowers the rank of the $(d+1)$-dimensional rigidity matroid. **The globally rigid graph bridge conjecture.** Under these hypotheses, $e$ is an $\mathcal{R}_{d+1}$-bridge in $G$. This is the globally rigid specialization of the linked-pairs dimension-dropping conjecture and remains open here.
object.source_name: Dániel Garamvölgyi and Tibor Jordán, “Minimally globally rigid graphs”, arXiv:2202.11617 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.11617

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2022).

object.title: The connectivity dimension-dropping conjecture for rigidity matroids
object.statement: Let $G$ be a graph and let $d$ be a positive integer. A graph is **redundantly $\mathcal{R}_d$-connected** when deleting any edge leaves it $\mathcal{R}_d$-connected. **The connectivity dimension-dropping conjecture.** If $G$ is $\mathcal{R}_{d+1}$-connected, then $G$ is redundantly $\mathcal{R}_d$-connected. A positive answer would strengthen the paper's dimension-dropping theorem and could help establish the linked-pairs dimension-dropping conjecture. The paper proves the two-dimensional instance but leaves the general statement open.
object.source_name: Dániel Garamvölgyi and Tibor Jordán, “Minimally globally rigid graphs”, arXiv:2202.11617 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.11617

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2022).

object.title: The rigidity-matroid bridge conjecture
object.statement: Let $d$ be a positive integer, let $G$ be an $\mathcal{R}_d$-connected graph, and let $e$ be an edge of $G$. An edge is an **$\mathcal{R}_{d+1}$-bridge** when its deletion lowers the rank of the $(d+1)$-dimensional rigidity matroid. **The rigidity-matroid bridge conjecture.** If $G-e$ is not $\mathcal{R}_d$-connected, then $e$ is an $\mathcal{R}_{d+1}$-bridge in $G$. The paper states that this is equivalent to the connectivity dimension-dropping conjecture, so it has the same significance and remains open in general.
object.source_name: Dániel Garamvölgyi and Tibor Jordán, “Minimally globally rigid graphs”, arXiv:2202.11617 (2022).

object.title: Pilaud–Santos conjecture on multit triangulations and rigidity matroids
object.statement: Let $k$-triangulations be the maximal graphs on $[n]$ with no $(k+1)$-crossing, and let the generic bar-and-joint rigidity matroid of dimension $2k$ be the matroid obtained from generic configurations of points in $\mathbb{R}^{2k}$ using the usual bar-and-joint rigidity matrix. **Pilaud–Santos conjecture.** $k$-triangulations are bases in the generic bar-and-joint rigidity matroid of dimension $2k$. The source states this as a conjecture of Pilaud and Santos; its relationship with the generic hyperconnectivity matroid is given, but the conjecture's resolution is not specified.
object.source_name: Luis Crespo Ruiz and Francisco Santos, “Multitriangulations and tropical Pfaffians”, arXiv:2203.04633 (2022).

object.title: Sufficiency of the R1--R4 relations for the recurrence proofs
object.statement: Let $S_m(\rho\mid\sigma)$ denote the finite-level $(z,q)$ sums, and let $R_1$--$R_4$ be the relations listed for the relevant moduli. **The R1--R4 sufficiency conjecture.** In each modulus, the relations $R_1$--$R_4$ are enough to prove the required recurrences. This asserts that the displayed relations form a complete proof mechanism for the recurrence systems in every modulus treated. The passage explicitly says that a full proof is not currently available, so the conjecture is open.
object.source_name: Shashank Kanade and Matthew C. Russell, “Completing the A_2 Andrews-Schilling-Warnaar identities”, arXiv:2203.05690 (2022).

object.title: Model-independent spanning conjecture for q-bracket spaces
object.statement:
Let $\mathcal{Z}_q$ be the q-bracket space associated with the partition-function framework, let $\mathbb{P}$ be the space of partition observables, and let $\mathscr{H}$ and $\mathscr{J}$ be the distinguished subspaces used in the setup. Write $\langle\mathbb{P}\rangle_q$ for the q-brackets generated by $\mathbb{P}$, and similarly for intersections with these subspaces.

**Model-independent q-bracket conjecture.** One has

$$
\mathcal{Z}_q=\langle\mathbb{P}\rangle_q=\langle\mathbb{P}\cap\mathscr{H}\rangle_q=\langle\mathbb{P}\cap\mathscr{J}\rangle_q.
$$

The conjecture reformulates the preceding Bernoulli–Seki reduction independently of the choice of model. The supplied text gives no resolution status, so whether these equalities hold remains open here.
object.source_name: Henrik Bachmann and Jan-Willem van Ittersum, “Partitions, Multiple Zeta Values and the q-bracket”, arXiv:2203.09165 (2023).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.09165

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2022).

object.title: Arc-disjoint hamiltonian paths in 2-generated Cayley digraphs of finite abelian groups
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, and let $\{a,b\}$ be a $2$-element generating set of $G$ whose elements $a$ and $b$ are nontrivial. Write

$$
\mathop{\mathsf{C}\mkern-1mu\overrightarrow{\mathsf{ay}}}(G;a,b)
$$

for the directed Cayley graph with generators $a$ and $b$.

**Finite abelian Cayley-digraph conjecture.** The digraph $\mathop{\mathsf{C}\mkern-1mu\overrightarrow{\mathsf{ay}}}(G;a,b)$ has two arc-disjoint hamiltonian paths.

This conjecture extends the result for Cartesian products of two directed cycles to finite abelian groups. The supplied text presents it as a natural expected extension, but gives no resolution for the full stated generality.

object.title: The uniqueness conjecture for consistent matroidal sandpile torsor algorithms
object.statement: Let $M=(E,\mathcal B,\chi)$ be an oriented regular matroid, let $(\sigma,\sigma^*)$ be a pair of acyclic signatures, and let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be matroidal sandpile torsor algorithms. Say that $\alpha$ and $\beta$ have the same **structure** when $\beta$ is one of $\alpha$, $\alpha'$, $\alpha”$, or $\alpha”'$, obtained by complementing the circuit and/or cocircuit signatures. **Uniqueness conjecture.** Every consistent matroidal sandpile torsor algorithm has the same structure as the Backman–Baker–Yuen algorithm. This is presented as an open conjecture alongside the conjecture that the Backman–Baker–Yuen algorithm itself is consistent; the authors caution that the consistency definition may require modification.
object.source_name: Ankan Ganguly and Alex McDonough, “Rotor-Routing Induces the Only Consistent Sandpile Torsor Structure on Plane Graphs”, arXiv:2203.15079 (2023).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.15079

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of March 2022). “This conjecture was independently proven by Ding as well as by Shokrieh and Wright . } However, both algorithms satisfy , and they both define the same sandpile torsor algorithm .”
